triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative closes 'to make single-letter rows a practical row spine for this part.' — 'this part' is the writer part (writer_part p07), workflow register barred by the Ps strategy §10 rule that row prose describes the text and that cross-row references are verse-anchored. E-18 arm: the claim the phrase carries re-derives TRUE from bytes. A verse-opener walk over verse_map_oshb.json for MT 37:1-40, with the title word set aside at MT 37:1 (Ps 37 is a titled IDENTITY psalm — verse_map_web.json marks Ps.37.0 title_is_prefix_of_mt_v1, rule 'identity', mt Ps.37.1, so the row's 'web:Ps.37.0 = oshb:Ps.37.1' is the mandated superscription form), realizes 20 of the 22 letters, at MT 37:1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21, 23, 25, 27, 30, 32, 34, 35 and 37 — a fresh letter about every two verses, exactly as the rival says; ayin stands at 0 of the 40 MT verse-openers and tav opens only MT 37:31 (non-structural), so both '20 of the 22 ... across the acrostic's 40 MT verses' and the device_notes ayin/tav asymmetry are byte-true. The row's own warrants also hold: its aleph and bet splices collate byte at oshb:Ps.37.1 and oshb:Ps.37.3, and MT 37:4 opens on a waw form, not a fresh letter, so 'web:Ps.37.4 continues the ב span' is correct. True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative routes a byte-true acrostic-density argument through a workflow part reference ('a practical row spine for this part') instead of describing the text.
findings.grounds: Quoted clause: 'to make single-letter rows a practical row spine for this part.' Ps strategy §10 bars part-range and workflow talk in row prose. The digits it carries re-derive true (20 realized letters across MT 37:1-40; ayin 0 of 40 verse-openers; tav only at MT 37:31), so nothing but the register is wrong.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, strongest_rejected_alternative, content and digits unchanged: '...but the psalm's acrostic letters recur too densely — a fresh structural letter about every two verses, 20 of the 22 letters realized across MT 37:1-40 — for single-letter rows to be a workable spine inside this psalm.'

triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads 'leaving web:Ps.37.8 to open the next row alone' — a positional row reference, barred by §10 ('cross-row references are verse-anchored'). E-18 arm: the reference is counterfactual (it describes the rejected re-grouping, not the shipped neighbour), so it carries no false claim about another row; the shipped next row M8-Ps-099 does open at web:Ps.37.9. Purely cosmetic -> low. The row's own digit claim, re-derived, stands: the verse-opener walk over MT 37:1-40 gives a 2-verse span for every realized letter EXCEPT dalet (MT 37:7 alone), kaf (MT 37:20 alone), qof (MT 37:34 alone), samekh (MT 37:27-29) and shin (MT 37:37-40) — exactly the five length-irregularities across 20 realized letters the row names — and its three openers are all imperatives (דּ֤וֹם at MT 37:7, הֶ֣רֶף at MT 37:8, and the gimel imperative at MT 37:5, each collated byte at its ref).

findings.claim: The rejected alternative locates a hypothetical seam by row position ('to open the next row alone') where §10 requires verse anchoring.
findings.grounds: Quoted from strongest_rejected_alternative; the shipped neighbour M8-Ps-099 does open at web:Ps.37.9, so the reference is cosmetic rather than false.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: '...leaving the seam at web:Ps.37.7|Ps.37.8 to carry he alone.'

findings.claim: The rival's sole rejection ground — that he's imperative 'reads as one clause with dalet's' — is not supported by the bytes, and a stronger byte warrant for the same four-verse grouping was available and uncited.
findings.grounds: MT 37:7 opens on the imperative דּ֤וֹם, runs a second imperative clause and then a prohibition; MT 37:8 opens asyndetically on the imperative הֶ֣רֶף — two verses of several clauses each with no syntactic joint, so 'one clause' is false at the grammar tier (both openers collate byte at their refs). What does bind them is lexical: the prohibition אַל תִּ֭תְחַר at MT 37:7 recurs as אַל תִּ֝תְחַ֗ר at MT 37:8 (sweep.py --skel, count unit verses: 3 verses in Psalms — MT 37:1, 37:7, 37:8, all inside this psalm), a real recurrence warrant for holding dalet and he in one row.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, strongest_rejected_alternative: replace 'reads as one clause with dalet's' with the recurrence warrant — e.g. '...but the prohibition that opened the acrostic recurs in both MT 37:7 and MT 37:8 (3 verses in Psalms, skeleton tier), holding dalet and he in one four-verse unit.'

triggers.grounds: Calibration holds; medium_low is honest and, if anything, conservative. Both seams stand at structural acrostic positions re-derived from bytes: kaf opens the row's first verse MT 37:20 on the particle כִּ֤י (collated byte at oshb:Ps.37.20) and nun opens MT 37:25 immediately past the row's close, so the outer bounds coincide with the complete letter groups kaf (37:20), lamed (37:21-22) and mem (37:23-24). The stated reason for the low band is byte-true: lamed לֹוֶ֣ה opens MT 37:21 one verse after kaf — one of the psalm's five length-irregularities (dalet, kaf and qof 1 verse; samekh 3; shin 4) — and the kaf position sits on a particle rather than a content word, precisely the surface/buried-letter caveat Ps strategy §2e requires for Ps 37. No cap applies (a strophe row inside a long psalm; the whole_psalm ruling is not in play) and no frontier flag is warranted. The band is not masking a byte-defective warrant — but the row does carry a separate byte-false position claim, recorded as a finding.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale says the plural 'the wicked' opens the span's first verse while citing the Hebrew token at oshb:Ps.37.20, but MT 37:20 opens on the kaf particle — the row's own acrostic warrant — with that plural standing second.
findings.grounds: MT 37:20 reads כִּ֤י, then רְשָׁעִ֨ים (both collated byte at oshb:Ps.37.20; word order taken from verse_map_oshb.json). The row asserts the opposite twice elsewhere — observed_substrate_signals ('surface כ at web:Ps.37.20 sits on the causal particle') and device_notes ('The surface letter at web:Ps.37.20 sits on the causal particle ... rather than a fresh content word') — so the claim contradicts the row's own driver in a psalm whose entire method is which word opens a verse. The position holds only of the WEB rendering ('But the wicked shall perish.'), i.e. a WEB word-order fact attached to an oshb-cited token.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, boundary_rationale, no span effect: '...and the related plural (oshb:Ps.37.20) stands as the second word of the span's first verse, web:Ps.37.20, immediately after the kaf particle' — or simply 'occurs in' for 'opens'.

findings.claim: The driver sentence claims the wicked-versus-righteous contrast runs 'across all 5 verses of the span', but MT 37:23-24 name no wicked party.
findings.grounds: MT 37:23 reads מֵ֭יְהוָה מִֽצְעֲדֵי גֶ֥בֶר כּוֹנָ֗נוּ (collated byte at oshb:Ps.37.23) and MT 37:24 continues the same upheld man; neither verse carries a wicked term, and the row's own parenthetical for web:Ps.37.23-24 glosses one side only. The contrast is byte-present at MT 37:20, 37:21 and 37:22.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: narrow to 'the wicked-versus-righteous contrast runs web:Ps.37.20-Ps.37.22, and web:Ps.37.23-Ps.37.24 continue the righteous side alone'.

triggers.grounds: Calibration holds. The row's closing seam falls inside tsade's two-verse group (MT 37:32-33) and the row discloses exactly that, with the same disclosure carried on the partner row M8-Ps-103's opening — a coherent seam pair, not a hidden defect — and medium_low is the honest band for a seam whose next verse depends on this one grammatically: MT 37:33 opens יְ֭הוָה לֹא יַעַזְבֶ֣נּוּ בְיָד֑וֹ, whose pronoun objects depend on the righteous named in צוֹפֶ֣ה רָ֭שָׁע לַצַּדִּ֑יק at MT 37:32 (both collated byte at their refs). Every structural claim re-derives true: pe opens MT 37:30 on פִּֽי צַ֭דִּיק and tsade opens MT 37:32, so 'pe before tsade, the regular alphabetic order' is byte-correct; the surface tsade at MT 37:29, צַדִּיקִ֥ים, is premature noise; ayin re-derives at 0 of the psalm's 40 MT verse-openers, absent from the whole surface table as the observed_substrate_signals states; and the aleph-noise cross-reference is byte-true (אֲדֹנָ֥י opens MT 37:13) and verse-anchored. Not a defect on the confidence lane.

findings.claim: device_notes closes on a positional row reference ('straddling this row's own closing seam with the row that follows') where §10 requires the cross-row reference to be verse-anchored; not caught by the OW-1 retro scan.
findings.grounds: Quoted from device_notes. The fact itself is byte-true — tsade's group runs MT 37:32-33 and MT 37:33's pronoun objects depend on the righteous named at MT 37:32 — so only the register is wrong, and §10 bars positional row references in row prose without exception.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, device_notes: '...tsade's full two-verse span runs MT 37:32-33, straddling the seam at web:Ps.37.32|Ps.37.33.'

triggers.grounds: Calibration holds; medium_low with an explicitly registered uncertainty is the honest band. The seam's stated warrant re-derives byte-true: MT 51:20 opens on the imperative הֵיטִ֣יבָה, and it is the only verse in Psalm 51 carrying Zion, walls or Jerusalem — a skeleton scan of MT 51:1-21 for those three objects returns 1 verse, MT 51:20 — so 'absent from the rest of the psalm' and both observed_substrate_signals digits ('sweep: 1 verse', twice) are true, and the quoted run צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם collates byte at oshb:Ps.51.20. Numbering is right for this shift+2 psalm: ps_lib.web_to_mt gives WEB 51:18 = MT 51:20 and WEB 51:19 = MT 51:21, exactly as the refs dual-cite, and the span closes the psalm. The low band is not masking a byte-defective warrant; the row's defects are register and numbering discipline, recorded separately.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative and device_notes narrate the authoring process rather than the text — 'is the mandated rival', 'The candidate holds it as its own unit', '(see observed_substrate_signals)', '(see rejected_alternative)'.
findings.grounds: All four phrases are quoted from strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes. §10 bars process narration and field/file-order talk in row prose; the substantive rival (the Zion petition as integral versus appended) and the holding are unaffected — only their framing is out of register.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: state the rival in text terms ('The closing couplet can be read as continuous with the vow-and-sacrifice unit before it, since both turn on sacrifice...') and drop the field cross-references, keeping the uncertainty statement.

findings.class: numbering discipline (bare refs inside a shift+2 psalm)
findings.claim: The rival sentence uses bare '51:18-19' and '51:13-17' with no numbering-space qualifier in a shift+2 psalm, where those same numbers denote different verses in MT — the very verses the rival contrasts.
findings.grounds: Ps 51 is one of the four +2 psalms (web_mt_offset_map.json; ps_lib.web_to_mt(51,18) = MT 51:20). MT 51:18 is כִּ֤י לֹא תַחְפֹּ֣ץ זֶ֣בַח (= WEB 51:16) and MT 51:19 is זִֽבְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ (= WEB 51:17) — the sacrifice-theology verses of the preceding row — so bare '51:18-19' resolves to the Zion petition only for a reader applying the bare-ref-is-WEB convention. Ps strategy §3 requires prose verse mentions to resolve against the row's psalm and be mirrored.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: write 'web:Ps.51.18-Ps.51.19 (= oshb:Ps.51.20-Ps.51.21)' and 'web:Ps.51.13-Ps.51.17 (= oshb:Ps.51.15-Ps.51.19)' in the rejected-alternative prose.

triggers.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative reads '...making it the true opener of the petition block that belongs to the next row, not this one's closer' — a positional row reference, barred by §10. E-18 arm: the claim re-derives TRUE. MT 58:7 opens on אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים הֲרָס (collated byte at oshb:Ps.58.7), and across all 12 MT verses of Psalm 58 it is the only verse opening on a divine-name vocative plus imperative: MT 58:1 is the title (lamnatseach, al-tashcheth, le-David, miktam — no historical note, as device_notes says) and the divine name at MT 58:12, אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים, is the subject of a verbal clause, not a vocative. The denominator is right for this shift+1 psalm (WEB 11 verses, MT 12; ps_lib.web_to_mt(58,1) = MT 58:2). The shipped next row M8-Ps-162 does open at web:Ps.58.6 = oshb:Ps.58.7 on that verse, and this row's close is independently warranted: MT 58:6 opens on the subordinate אֲשֶׁ֣ר (byte at oshb:Ps.58.6), completing the cobra figure inside the span rather than starting new material. True claim carried in workflow register -> low, cosmetic.

findings.claim: The rejected alternative anchors its (byte-true) petition-block claim to row position ('belongs to the next row, not this one's closer') where §10 requires verse anchoring.
findings.grounds: Quoted from strongest_rejected_alternative; the underlying facts re-derive true (MT 58:7 is the only vocative-plus-imperative opener among the psalm's 12 MT verses; the subordinate clause opening MT 58:6 closes this row's figure), so the defect is register only.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: '...making oshb:Ps.58.7 (= web:Ps.58.6) the opener of the petition block that begins past the seam web:Ps.58.5|Ps.58.6, not this unit's closer.'

triggers.grounds: Confirmed: the tier-4 fact does seam work in two places. (1) boundary_rationale opens 'Past the oracle's closing quotation mark at the end of web:Ps.60.8 (oshb:Ps.60.10), this unit opens with...' — WEB punctuation is the locator for the row's own opening seam. (2) observed_substrate_signals #1 records the same punctuation as a substrate signal: 'Interrogative resumption at web:Ps.60.9 (oshb:Ps.60.11) sits outside the oracle's WEB quotation marks.' The punctuation is real in the WEB bytes (verse_map_web.json: the opening curly quote sits mid-verse in WEB 60:6 after 'God has spoken from his sanctuary:', the closing curly quote ends WEB 60:8, and WEB 60:9 carries none), but translation punctuation is tier-4 — never boundary evidence, never counter-evidence by absence, and not a substrate signal at all. This is neither a disclosure nor a stray descriptive remark. The seam does, however, have an independent tier-1 warrant that the row half-states: the divine first-person oracle closes at MT 60:10, the psalmist's own interrogative opens MT 60:11, מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי (collated byte at oshb:Ps.60.11), and MT 60:12 addresses God in the second person, so the speaker shift stands in the Hebrew independently of the translation's quotation marks. Corroboration of a tier-1-warranted seam -> medium, not high. Numbering is clean for this shift+2 psalm: ps_lib.web_to_mt gives 60:8 = MT 60:10, 60:9 = MT 60:11 and 60:12 = MT 60:14, and WEB Ps 60 does close at its twelfth verse (MT 60:14 last).

findings.class: E-23 tier-4 (WEB punctuation) carried as seam evidence
findings.claim: The row's opening seam is framed by, and its first substrate signal consists of, the WEB oracle's closing quotation mark — tier-4 translation punctuation doing seam work, corroborating a seam that does have an independent Hebrew speaker-shift warrant.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale's leading clause and observed_substrate_signals #1, both quoted in the trigger grounds; verse_map_web.json confirms the curly quote opening mid-verse in WEB 60:6, closing at the end of WEB 60:8, and absent from WEB 60:9. The available tier-1 warrant: divine first-person speech through MT 60:10 against the psalmist's interrogative מִ֣י יֹ֭בִלֵנִי at MT 60:11 (byte tier) and the second-person address to God at MT 60:12.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair, no span effect: lead boundary_rationale with the speaker shift standing in the bytes (the oracle's first-person divine speech closing at oshb:Ps.60.10 against the psalmist's interrogative at oshb:Ps.60.11 and the second-person address at oshb:Ps.60.12), and either delete observed_substrate_signals #1 or re-cast it as an explicit tier-4 non-evidential disclosure. Seam-pair note for the adjudicator: the partner row M8-Ps-168 argues the same seam on the same quotation marks (its boundary_rationale makes the curly quotation the speaker-shift marker), so under §10 any cure is one edit installed on both rows.

triggers.grounds: Confirmed — one tag, two matches, both in boundary_rationale: 'continuing the rock vocabulary of the prior row's close' and 'echoes the prior row's own close', positional row references barred by §10. E-18 arm: the claim they carry re-derives TRUE. צ֭וּרִי stands in MT 62:7 (= web:Ps.62.6, the last verse of the shipped previous row) and this row's opening verse MT 62:8 carries צוּר עֻזִּ֥י, both collated byte at their refs, so the rock vocabulary does continue across the seam. True claim in workflow register -> low; the cure is verse anchoring. The row's other numbers hold: the dual-cites are right for this shift+1 psalm (ps_lib.web_to_mt: 62:7 = MT 62:8 through 62:12 = MT 62:13), and Selah is word-bound at MT 62:5 and MT 62:9 only — 2 verses — so 'the psalm's later of 2 Selah instances (sweep: 2 verses); no further Selah in web:Ps.62.9-web:Ps.62.12' is byte-true and satisfies the §2d span-scoped symmetry.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale twice locates its (byte-true) continuity claim by row position ('the prior row's close') where §10 requires verse anchoring.
findings.grounds: Both phrases quoted from boundary_rationale; the fact re-derives true — צ֭וּרִי at MT 62:7 and צוּר עֻזִּ֥י at MT 62:8, each collated byte at its ref.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: '...continuing the rock vocabulary of oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6) across the seam web:Ps.62.6|Ps.62.7...' and '...echoes oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6).'

findings.class: seam warrant absent from the row (warrant locality)
findings.claim: The row states no warrant standing at its own opening seam — it concedes continuity there and places its driver one verse inside the span — yet carries confidence high; the tier-1 fact that does hold the seam sits only on the partner row.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'This unit opens still in first-person voice, continuing the rock vocabulary...'; its stated driver, the plural imperative בִּטְח֘וּ addressed to the people, עָ֗ם, stands at MT 62:9 = web:Ps.62.8, one verse inside the span, and the rejected alternative rejects 'Ps.62.7-62.8 as a continuation' on that same shift, which does not reach web:Ps.62.7. The seam is nevertheless sound, so no respan is proposed: Psalm 62 is on the §6 refrain roster and its refrain returns at MT 62:7, whose first three words, אַךְ ה֣וּא צ֭וּרִי, repeat the opening of MT 62:3 byte-for-byte (each run collates byte at its own ref, and the two runs are string-identical; the partner row calls the same match skeleton tier, understating it), so the preceding unit closes on the refrain return and this unit opens past it. That warrant is carried by M8-Ps-172's observed_substrate_signals, not by this row.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair on this row, no respan: add the seam's own warrant, verse-anchored — 'the unit begins past the psalm's refrain return at oshb:Ps.62.7 (= web:Ps.62.6), which repeats the opening of oshb:Ps.62.3' — and keep the register shift at oshb:Ps.62.9 as the unit's driver; the adjudicator may also weigh whether high survives without it.
